Error Detection  
Error Detection  
Directions: Read each sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The  
error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Mark the part with the error as your answer. If  
there is no error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any).  
Q1. It may be possible to do (A)/a field enumeration who (B)/can mark any group under (C)/castes  
found in the available OBC/BC lists (D).  
A. It may be possible to do  
B. a field enumeration who  
C. can mark any group under  
D. found in the available OBC/BC lists  
E. No error  
Answer: B. a field enumeration who  
Explanation:  
Since we are not talking about a person, ‘who’ is incorrect. Here, ‘that’ is correct because it specifies a  
particular thing.  
It may be possible to do a field enumeration that can mark any group under castes found in the  
available OBC/BC lists.  
Q2. In front, at a weary gallop (A)/and using his leather whip, (B)/rode an officer, dishevelled and  
drenched, (C)/whom trousers had worked up to above his knees (D).  
A. In front, at a weary gallop  
B. and using his leather whip  
C. rode an officer, disheveled and drenched  
D. whom trousers had worked up to above his knees  
E. No error  
Answer: D. whom trousers had worked up to above his knees  
Explanation:  
Here, the possessive relative pronoun ‘whose’ is correct.  
In front, at a weary gallop and using his leather whip, rode an officer, dishevelled and drenched, whose  
trousers had worked up to above his knees.  
2
Error Detection  
Q3. But on the road, the highroad along that the troops marched, (A)/there was no such freshness even  
at night or when the road passed (B)/through the forest; the dew was imperceptible on the (C)/ sandy  
dust churned up more than six inches deep (D).  
A. But on the road, the highroad along that the troops marched  
B. there was no such freshness even at night or when the road passed  
C. through the forest; the dew was imperceptible on the  
D. sandy dust churned up more than six inches deep  
E. No error  
Answer: A. But on the road, the highroad along that the troops marched  
Explanation:  
Here, ‘that’ is incorrect, instead ‘which’ is correct.  
But on the road, the highroad along which the troops marched, there was no such freshness even at  
night or when the road passed through the forest; the dew was imperceptible on the sandy dust  
churned up more than six inches deep.  
Q4. Eadberht showed considerable independence in his dealings (A)/with the church, and his brother  
Ecgberht, (B)/to who the well-known letter of Bede is addressed, (C)/was from 734 to 766 archbishop of  
York (D).  
A. Eadberht showed considerable independence in his dealings  
B. with the church, and his brother Ecgberht  
C. to who the well-known letter of Bede is addressed  
D. was from 734 to 766 archbishop of York  
E. No error  
Answer: C. to who the well-known letter of Bede is addressed  
Explanation: Here, the object pronoun, ‘whom’ is correct.  
Eadberht showed considerable independence in his dealings with the church, and his brother Ecgberht,  
to whom the well-known letter of Bede is addressed, was from 734 to 766 archbishop of York.

Answer: C. out there who would still pay  
Explanation:  
Here, the subject pronoun ‘who’ is correct.  
Sure, the million-dollar offer was withdrawn but I'll bet there are thousands of people out there who  
would still pay a fortune to own the artifact.  
Q6. To the former he owes his appreciation of exact investigation (A)/and a complete knowledge of the

(E) No error

Q7. Each provincial administrative junta is composed, in part, (A)/of government nominees, and in

Answer: D  
Explanation:

Instead, the object pronoun ‘whom’ is correct.

Q11. There are several auditor and investment manager (A)/ in the state whose services may be (B)/  
availed off by the state police (C)/ whether to train a set of personnel or to develop (D)/a stream to deal  
only into economic offenses (E).  
(A) A  
(B) C  
(C) D  
(D) E  
(E) All are correct  
Answer: 3  
Explanation:  
A- Here, since ‘several’ is used, ‘auditors and managers’ should have been used.  
C- The phrase ‘availed of’ will be correct, not ‘availed off’. ‘Avail yourself of something’ means ‘to make  
use of something’.  
E- The phrase ‘deal with something’ will be correct. The phrase used here, ‘deal only into’ does not give  
a comprehensive meaning.  
There are several auditors and investment managers in the state whose services may be availed of  
by the state police whether to train a set of personnel or to develop a stream to deal only with  
economic offenses.  
Q12. The decision came in the awake of (A)/a compliant received by the health ministry (B)/about  
ineligible beneficiaries faking their identity (C)/as health and frontline workers (D)/ to register  
vaccination (E).  
(A) A  
(B) B  
(C) C  
(D) E  
(E) All are correct  
6
Error Detection  
Answer: 3  
Explanation:  
A- The phrase ‘in the awake of’ is incorrect. The correct phrase is ‘in the wake of’. ‘If something  
happens in the wake of something else, it happens after and often because of it’.  
B- The word ‘compliant’ is wrong in this context. It means ‘disposed to agree with others or obey rules,  
especially to an excessive degree’. The correct word which should have been used here is ‘complaint’.  
E- The preposition ‘for’ should be used before ‘vaccination’ in order to make the phrase grammatically  
correct.  
The decision came in the wake of complaints received by the health ministry about ineligible  
beneficiaries faking their identity as health and frontline workers to register for vaccination.  
Q13. The last times India’s seven-day average (A)/of daily cases was the highest in the world (B)/was  
for October 19 last year, (C)/before a massive surge in cases make (D)/the US the world’s leading  
coronavirus hotspot (E).  
(A) A  
(B) B  
(C) C  
(D) D  
(E) All are correct  
Answer: 2  
Explanation:  
A- Since we are talking about one particular point of time, ‘last times’ is incorrect, and should be  
replaced by ‘last time’.  
C- The date is specified. So, ‘on’ is the correct preposition, and not ‘for’.  
D- The word ‘make’ does not comply with the tense. It should be replaced with ‘made’.  
The last time India’s seven-day average of daily cases was the highest in the world was on October 19  
last year, before a massive surge in cases made the US the world’s leading coronavirus hotspot.

Error Detection  
Q14. All ships stranded by the grounding of (A)/ the giant container ship Ever Given (B)/in the Suez  
Canal in March had passed away (C)/the canal though Saturday, ending the backlog (D)/that built up  
among the blockage (E).  
(A) A  
(B) C  
(C) D  
(D) E  
(E) All are correct  
Answer: 1  
Explanation:  
C- The phrase ‘pass away’ means ‘die’. The correct phrase here is ‘passed through the canal’.  
D- The word ‘though’ is inappropriate at that place. The correct word is ‘on’ or ‘by’.  
E- Here, the word ‘among’ is incorrect. The ships passed through the canal ending the backlog created  
at the time of the blockage. So, instead of ‘among’, ‘during’ is more appropriate.  
All ships stranded by the grounding of the giant container ship Ever Given in the Suez Canal in March  
had passed through the canal by Saturday, ending the backlog that built up during the blockage.  
Q15. Prosecutors in Taiwan sought an arrest warrant (A)/for the honour of an unmanned truck

(A) B  
(B) C  
(C) D

Explanation:  
B- The word ‘honour’ is inappropriate here. The correct word should be ‘owner’.  
D- Th preposition ‘for’ will give a wrong meaning of the sentence. The correct preposition is ‘in’.

Q16. Britain’s medicine regulator are urging people (A)/to continue taking Astra Zeneca coronavirus  
vaccine, (B)/despite revealing this seven people (C)/in the UK have died in (D)/rare blood clots after  
getting the jab (E).  
(A) A  
(B) B  
(C) C  
(D) D  
(E) All are correct  
Answer: 2  
Explanation:  
A- Since ‘regulator’ is a single person, ‘is’ should be used, not ‘are’.  
C- The word ‘this’ does not fit in here, because, these seven people are not mentioned in the sentence  
before. So, it should be replaced with ‘that’.  
D- Here, rather that using ‘in’, ‘from’ is more suitable. ‘Died from rare blood clots’ is correct.  
Britain’s medicine regulator is urging people to continue taking Astra Zeneca coronavirus vaccine,  
despite revealing that seven people in the UK have died from rare blood clots after getting the jab.  
Q17. Two months after the (A)/Taliban takeover on Kabul, (B)/New Delhi be planning (C)/to engaged  
regional powers (D)/on the future of Afghanistan (E).  
(A) B  
(B) C  
(C) D  
(D) E  
(E) All are correct.  
Answer: 4  
Explanation:  
B- the word ‘takeover’ means ‘an act of taking control of something’. ‘takeover on something’ is  
incorrect. The correct preposition must be ‘of’.  
C- here the verb ‘be’ is incorrect. Instead, ‘is’ is correct.  
D- here, ‘to engaged’ is grammatically incorrect. Instead, ‘to engage’ must be used.  
Two months after the Taliban takeover of Kabul, New Delhi is planning to engage regional powers on  
the future of Afghanistan.

(D) E

Q22. I. The traditional education system has long been criticised for curbing a student’s natural creative  
ability.  
II. New tools and innovations also help make online learning more user-friendly, provide more space for  
experimentation and expose learners to new ideas.  
III. Technologies such as 3D videos, simulations and augmented reality have created an immersive  
experience for learners and enabled the sharing of knowledges and informations in creative and  
dynamic ways.  
(A) Only II is incorrect  
(B) Only III is incorrect  
(C) Both I and II are incorrect  
(D) Both II and III are incorrect  
(E) All are incorrect  
Answer: B. Only III is incorrect  
Explanation: The word ‘informations’ is incorrect. The plural of ‘information’ is ‘information’. Also, here,  
the word ‘knowledge’ should have been used and not ‘knowledges’, as it is an uncountable noun and  
does not have singular or plural forms.  
The correct statement would be: Technologies such as 3D videos, simulations and augmented reality  
have created an immersive experience for learners and enabled the sharing of knowledge and  
information in creative and dynamic ways.  
Q23. I. The most impactful applications of responsible ML will come in how we apply our learnings to

II. The move comes at a time when several users criticised the platform over its image-cropping  
feature.  
III. Twitter is hardly the first social network to be accused in racial discrimination on the platform.  
(A) Only I is incorrect  
(B) Only II is incorrect  
(C) Both I and III are incorrect  
(D) Both II and III are incorrect  
(E) All are incorrect  
12  
Error Detection  
Answer: C. Both I and III are incorrect  
Explanation:  
I- Here, the preposition ‘in’ is incorrect. It should be ‘from’.  
The correct statement would be:  
The most impactful applications of responsible ML will come from how we apply our learnings to build a  
better Twitter.  
III- The preposition ‘in’ after ‘accused’ is incorrect. The correct preposition is ‘of’. ‘Accused of  
something’ is the correct usage.  
The correct statement is:  
Twitter is hardly the first social network to be accused of racial discrimination on the platform.  
Q24. I. Translation tools from Alphabet Inc's Google and other companies could be contributing to  
significant misunderstanding of legal terms with conflicting meanings such as "enjoin," according to  
research due to be presented at an academic workshop.  
II. The new paper rises concerns about a popular method companies use to broaden the vocabulary of  
their translation software.  
III. Researchers previously have found programs that learn translations by studying non-diverse text  
perpetuate historical gender biases, such as associating "doctor" with "he."  
(A) Only I is incorrect  
(B) Only II is incorrect  
(C) Both I and II are incorrect  
(D) Both II and III are incorrect  
(E) All are incorrect  
Answer: B. Only II is incorrect  
Explanation:  
II- The word ‘rises’ should be replaced by the word ‘raises’.  
When something ‘rises’, it does it on its own power. ‘Rises’ is an intransitive verb, meaning there is no  
object that accompanies it.  
On the other hand, when something ‘raises’, it's a transitive verb that is followed by an object.  
The sentence can be rephrased correctly as:  
The new paper raises concerns about a popular method companies use to broaden the vocabulary of  
their translation software.

Q58. It may be possible to do (A)/a field enumeration who (B)/can mark any group under (C)/castes  
found in the available OBC/BC lists (D).  
(A) It may be possible to do  
(B) a field enumeration who  
(C) can mark any group under  
(D) found in the available OBC/BC lists  
(E) No error  
Answer: B  
Explanation:  
Since we are not talking about a person, ‘who’ is incorrect. Here, ‘that’ is correct because it specifies a  
particular thing.  
It may be possible to do a field enumeration that can mark any group under castes found in the  
available OBC/BC lists.  
Q59. In front, at a weary gallop (A)/and using his leather whip, (B)/rode an officer, dishevelled and

(B) and using his leather whip  
(C) rode an officer, disheveled and drenched  
(D) whom trousers had worked up to above his knees  
(E) No error  
Answer: D  
Explanation:  
Here, the possessive relative pronoun ‘whose’ is correct.  
In front, at a weary gallop and using his leather whip, rode an officer, dishevelled and drenched, whose  
trousers had worked up to above his knees.

Q60. But on the road, the highroad along that the troops marched, (A)/there was no such freshness

(D) which has been appointed only now  
(E) No error

Q69. To resolve issues that have cropped up between itself (A)/and the department of financial  
services within the finance ministry (B)/on the issue of valuation of ATI bonds, market regulator Sebi  
(C)/provided that another way to value these instruments (D).  
(A) To resolve issues that have cropped up between itself  
(B) and the department of financial services within the finance ministry  
(C) on the issue of valuation of ATI bonds, market regulator Sebi  
(D) provided that another way to value these instruments  
(E) No error  
Answer: D  
39  
Error Detection  
Explanation:  
The preposition ‘that’ is unnecessary with the verb ‘provided’. It should be removed. The meaning of the  
phrase ‘provided that’ is ‘if, or only if’.  
To resolve issues that have cropped up between itself and the department of financial services within  
the finance ministry on the issue of valuation of ATI bonds, market regulator Sebi provided another  
way to value these instruments.  
Q70. Many ears will be cooked to hear (A)/the president essay an address (B)/crafted by Vinay Reddy,  
Biden’s chief speechwriter, whose job is (C)/to translate the president’s ideas into words (D).  
(A) Many ears will be cooked to hear  
(B) the president essay an address  
(C) crafted by Vinay Reddy, Biden’s chief speechwriter, whose job is  
(D) to translate the president’s ideas into words  
(E) No error  
Answer: A  
Explanation:  
The word ‘cooked’ is incorrect.  
The correct word should be ‘cocked’. To cock your ear means to listen very carefully. It should be used  
here.  
Many ears will be cocked to hear the president essay an address crafted by Vinay Reddy, Biden’s  
chief speechwriter, whose job is to translate the president’s ideas into words.
